showcases.title:
Four connected offerings
for practical AI transformation
showcases.subtitle: Team capability provides capacity, AI use cases create business value, and portfolio discipline protects investment focus. A parallel studio validates priority ideas without disrupting the roadmap.

pillars.label: Offering 1
pillars.title: Agentic AI for high-performing teams
pillars.subTitle: Capacity grows when AI becomes part of the team's operating system.
pillars.description: We identify repeatable tasks, define reusable context and guardrails, coach managers and teams, and measure whether adoption improves speed and quality without weakening accountability. Agents accelerate production. People own intent, evidence and release decisions.
pillars.tools: Context, Plan, Build, Verify, Release & learn

bullets.title: Engineering workflow
bullets.description: Planning, coding, test creation, review preparation, documentation and release readiness.

bullets.title: Manager workflow
bullets.description: Coaching preparation, risk synthesis, decision records, dependency visibility and status communication.

bullets.title: Operating model
bullets.description: Role clarity, guardrails, reusable agents, context standards and explicit human approvals.

bullets.title: Adoption system
bullets.description: Hands-on enablement, champions, usage measures, quality measures and continuous improvement.

bullets.title: The agentic delivery system
bullets.description: The organization supplies trusted context (product intent, architecture, standards). Agents help plan and produce work (work breakdown, code, tests, documentation). Automated checks, human review and security collect evidence at human gates, and a release owner approves controlled rollout. The learn stage turns telemetry and lessons into better reusable context.

pillars.label: Offering 2
pillars.title: AI in workflows and products
pillars.subTitle: Reduce friction in internal work. Create useful customer capabilities.
pillars.description: We separate workflow AI from product AI because the users, controls and value measures differ. In both cases, the work starts with a real decision or task, then connects data, experience design, architecture and evaluation to a production path.
pillars.tools: Data rights, Security, Evaluation, Human override, Monitoring, Cost

pillars.label: Offering 3
pillars.title: Portfolio priorities
pillars.subTitle: Every demand competes for the same constrained capacity.
pillars.description: The portfolio process puts unlike work on a common decision basis without pretending every item is identical. Leaders see the evidence, constraints and strategic trade-offs, then record what moves now, next, later or stops. The scoring model and weights are co-designed with the client.
pillars.tools: Business impact, Urgency & risk, Strategic fit, Effort & dependencies, Learning value

bullets.title: Customer demand
bullets.description: Revenue, retention, commitments and market urgency.

bullets.title: Technical debt
bullets.description: Reliability, security, compliance and developer friction.

bullets.title: Modernization
bullets.description: Architecture, platforms, cloud and data foundations.

bullets.title: Innovation
bullets.description: AI opportunities, new products and business experiments.

bullets.title: Now · Next · Later · Stop
bullets.description: The decision output includes capacity allocation, assumptions, milestones and explicit review dates.

bullets.title: A decision system leaders can defend
bullets.description: Evidence (customer and market signal, operational and quality data, architecture and security risk, cost and dependency facts) feeds trade-offs (comparable scoring, capacity scenarios, dependency map, risk and learning assumptions). Each decision records a priority and owner, expected outcome, funding and milestone, and a review, scale or stop date. Governance reviews changed evidence, resolves trade-offs and retires stale commitments.

pillars.label: Offering 4
pillars.title: Parallel innovation studio
pillars.subTitle: Validate strategic ideas without pulling delivery teams off committed work.
pillars.description: The studio creates a parallel lane staffed for discovery, design and proof. The committed roadmap continues while existing experts contribute in bounded workshops and review gates instead of becoming the POC team. Each engagement ends with evidence and an explicit scale, revise, handoff or stop decision.

about.avatarAlt: Jason Zhu, Principal Technology Consultant & AI Strategy Advisor
about.subtitle: Experience behind the offering
aboutParagraphs: Jason Zhu is the Principal Technology Consultant & AI Strategy Advisor at HealthDots Solutions, with 25+ years building and leading software organizations.

He has led a 50+ person engineering organization across product, platform and operations, helped scale AdjudiCare through 4× revenue growth while sustaining 99.9%+ availability, and reduced engineering costs by 30%+ through platform modernization and operating changes.
His Director and VP of Engineering experience is now applied through independent technology and AI advisory work, spanning healthcare, insurance, cloud platforms, AI adoption and regulated delivery.
The result is strategy grounded in hands-on architecture, delivery and organizational leadership.
